## Role in the Rating Process

The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) provides bright-line inputs to the [Backstop Eligibility](../parameters/backstop-eligibility.qmd) parameter (R6) through its debt-sustainability analysis and risk classification. It supplies the gross financing need cross-check for [Refinancing Need](../parameters/refinancing-need.qmd) (R1) via its [Debt Sustainability Monitor](../document-types/debt-sustainability-monitor.qmd). The institution runs fiscal surveillance, including assessments under the excessive deficit procedure, which informs [Fiscal Capacity](../parameters/fiscal-capacity.qmd) (C3-T*) and [Backstop Eligibility](../parameters/backstop-eligibility.qmd) (R6). It publishes the AMECO database, which serves as a source for unit-labour-cost and real-exchange-rate data relevant to [Growth](../parameters/growth.qmd) (C1-A2*) and [Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd) (C2-M*).

## Evidence by Country

### Euro Area

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assesses countries under the EU fiscal framework, monitoring compliance with net expenditure growth rates and the implementation of national medium-term fiscal-structural plans. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3-5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3-5">ⓘ</button>
- The institution evaluates the activation of the "national escape clause" for defense spending across several member states, permitting deviations from fiscal rules provided fiscal sustainability is not endangered in the medium term. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) published the [Debt Sustainability Monitor](../document-types/debt-sustainability-monitor.qmd) 2025, classifying medium-term fiscal sustainability risks for 12 Member States as high, 10 as medium, and 5 as low, based on a no-fiscal-policy-change baseline. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 11" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assessed the fiscal sustainability condition for activating the national escape clause for 16 Member States. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) forecasts that EU GDP growth will slow to 1.1% in 2026 and the Euro area to 0.9%, due to an energy price shock from the Middle East conflict. Growth is projected to recover to 1.4% (EU) and 1.2% (Euro area) in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 18" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 18">ⓘ</button>
- The aggregate EU general government deficit is projected to widen from 3.1% of GDP in 2025 to 3.6% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 22" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 22">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) notes that fiscal space is narrower than in 2022, with many Member States burdened by legacy costs and rising defense expenditure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 25" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) issued the Spring 2026 European Economic Forecast and provided a toolbox to address the energy crisis, emphasizing targeted and temporary fiscal measures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 80" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 80">ⓘ</button>

### [Austria](../countries/austria.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary deficit of 1.6% of GDP as of 2026, assuming no fiscal policy change from 2027. This level is low compared with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to increase. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 217" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 217">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 debt-stabilisation indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 4.2 percentage point improvement in the structural primary balance by 2027 to stabilize debt. This is driven by the initial budgetary position (2.3 pps) and ageing costs (1.8 pps). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 218" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 218">ⓘ</button>
- The S1 debt-reduction indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 3.7 percentage point effort to reduce debt to 60% of GDP by 2070. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 218" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 218">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected to remain large, reaching around 21% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 217" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 217">ⓘ</button>
- A large share of debt is held by non-residents. Contingent liability risks stem from the private sector and state guarantees. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 218" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 218">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 28 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 219" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 219">ⓘ</button>

### [Belgium](../countries/belgium.qmd)

- The structural primary balance is projected at -2.3% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 19.7% of GDP in 2025 and are projected to remain elevated. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) notes the activation of the national escape clause (NEC) for Belgium. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 debt-stabilisation indicator signals high risk, requiring a 7.0% of GDP improvement in the structural primary balance in 2027 to stabilize debt long-term. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 123" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 123">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund was 51 bps at the end of 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 122" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 122">ⓘ</button>
- Under the "Fragmented Action" climate scenario, debt could be around 3 percentage points of GDP higher in 2050 compared to the baseline. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109">ⓘ</button>
- GDP growth is expected to decelerate to 0.7% in 2026 and rebound to 0.9% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 108" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 108">ⓘ</button>
- The general government deficit is projected to stabilize at 5.2% in 2026 and rise to 5.4% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 109">ⓘ</button>
- The debt-to-GDP ratio is projected to increase to 112.8% by 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 109">ⓘ</button>

### [Bulgaria](../countries/bulgaria.qmd)

- The S2 indicator points to low risk, requiring only a 1.4% of GDP improvement in 2027 to stabilize debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 128" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 128">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) notes the activation of the national escape clause (NEC) for Bulgaria. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund was 112 bps at the end of 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 127" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 127">ⓘ</button>

- The government deficit is set to exceed 4% of GDP, reaching 4.1% in 2026 and 4.3% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 110" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 110">ⓘ</button>

### [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) provided “technical information” at the country’s request, aligning with the medium-term fiscal-structural plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 23" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 23">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) reported that Croatia’s economy grew by 3.4% in 2025, with inflation at 4.4%, significantly above the euro-area average. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission noted that the general government deficit widened to narrowly exceed the 3% of GDP threshold in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 42">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assessed Croatia’s implementation of Country-Specific Recommendations and activated the National Escape Clause for defence spending in coordination with the Council. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35, p. 42">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission highlighted challenges in fiscal consolidation, high unit labour costs, and structural issues such as fragmented public administration. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s Spring 2026 Forecast projected real GDP growth of 2.7% in 2026 and 2.5% in 2027, following actual growth of 3.4% in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The general government deficit increased from 2.3% of GDP in 2024 to 3.0% in 2025. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projected the deficit to decrease to 2.9% in 2026 and 2.7% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- Net expenditure grew by 10.9% in 2025, exceeding the recommended maximum growth rate. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 4-5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 4-5">ⓘ</button>
- The [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd) allowed [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd) to activate the national escape clause for defense spending in 2025-2028. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- The fiscal stance was expansionary by 1.6% of GDP in 2025. It is projected to be contractionary by 0.3% of GDP in 2026 and 0.9% of GDP in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd) adopted temporary fiscal measures to mitigate the impact of high energy prices following the war in the Middle East in February 2026. The projected fiscal cost is 0.1% of GDP in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- General government debt decreased from 57.4% of GDP at the end of 2024 to 56.3% at the end of 2025. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projected a further decline to 55.9% in 2026 and 55.6% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd) endorsed [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd)'s national medium-term fiscal-structural plan for 2025-2028. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at -1.7% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 12.6% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- GDP growth is expected to moderate to 2.7% in 2026 and 2.5% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 124" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 124">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary deficit of 1.7% of GDP as of 2026. This is in line with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to decrease slightly. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 172" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 172">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to low risk, requiring a 1.5 percentage point improvement in the structural primary balance by 2027. The S1 indicator also points to low risk, requiring a 1.3 percentage point effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 173" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 173">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected to amount to just above 12% of GDP over 2026-2027, reaching 14% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 172" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 172">ⓘ</button>
- The net international investment position (NIIP) adjusted for non-defaultable instruments reached +23.8% of GDP in Q3 2024. Financing sources are broadly stable. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 173" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 173">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 33 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 174" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 174">ⓘ</button>

### [Cyprus](../countries/cyprus.qmd)

- The structural primary balance is projected at 3.3% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 1.4% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- Real GDP is projected to grow by 2.3% in 2026 and 2.7% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 128" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 128">ⓘ</button>
- The general government surplus is projected to ease to 2.1% of GDP in 2026 and 2.5% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 129" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 129">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary surplus of 3.3% of GDP as of 2026. This is ambitious compared with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to increase significantly. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 182" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 182">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to low risk, requiring a 0.1 percentage point improvement. The S1 indicator points to low risk, with no fiscal effort required to keep debt below 60% of GDP by 2070. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 183" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 183">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected to decrease, dwindling to 0.4% of GDP by 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 182" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 182">ⓘ</button>
- Substantial cash reserves exist. The share of short-term public debt is low. Financing sources are stable with a diversified investor base. Debt is exclusively denominated in euro. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 183" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 183">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 19 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 184" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 184">ⓘ</button>

### [Estonia](../countries/estonia.qmd)
