- Gross financing needs were 2.7% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) notes the activation of the national escape clause (NEC) for Estonia. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund was 57 bps at the end of 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 147" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 147">ⓘ</button>
- Real GDP is projected to grow by 1.6% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 114" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 114">ⓘ</button>
- The general government deficit is set to widen to 4.5% of GDP in 2026 and 4.8% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 115" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 115">ⓘ</button>

### [Finland](../countries/finland.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) stated that Finland’s economy is emerging from stagnation and is expected to transit to broad-based growth in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reported that an excessive deficit procedure was opened in January 2026, although it is held in abeyance due to the activation of a national escape clause for increased defence spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission projected the general government deficit to rise to 4.5% in 2026 and 4.6% in 2027, with public debt increasing to 93.1% by 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assessed the implementation of Country-Specific Recommendations and the degree of compliance with the EU fiscal framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 27-31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 27-31">ⓘ</button>
- The document referenced [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) data and policies, such as the European Union fiscal framework and the European Union's Restoration Regulation. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 116" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 116">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s assessment and the [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)'s projections highlighted the need for continued fiscal consolidation to ensure debt sustainability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at -0.9% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 20.1% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- Long-term fiscal sustainability risks are medium. The S2 indicator signals that Finland would need to improve its structural primary balance by 4.1 percentage points to ensure debt stabilizes over the long term. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 248" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 248">ⓘ</button>
- The S1 indicator shows that a fiscal effort of 3.1 percentage points would be needed to reduce debt to 60% of GDP by 2070. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 248" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 248">ⓘ</button>
- Financial markets’ perceptions of sovereign risk have remained broadly stable, except for a downgrade by Fitch in July 2025 to the third highest rating, ‘AA’. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 247" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 247">ⓘ</button>
- Real GDP growth is projected to accelerate to 0.8% in 2026 and 1.4% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 148" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 148">ⓘ</button>
- The general government deficit is forecast to widen from 3.4% of GDP in 2025 to 4.5% in 2026 and 4.6% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 149" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 149">ⓘ</button>

### [France](../countries/france.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projected real GDP growth to remain subdued at 0.8% in both 2025 and 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reported that the general government deficit is projected to remain at 5.1% of GDP in 2026, with debt-to-GDP rising to a projected 118.1% in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assessed France’s status under the Excessive Deficit Procedure, which is currently held in abeyance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 40, p. 45" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 40, p. 45">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assessed the implementation of Country-Specific Recommendations and the progress of the Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- Simulations by the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) suggested that linking retirement age to life expectancy could reduce public pension expenditure by 1.0 percentage point of GDP by 2070. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projections were used to estimate the evolution of ageing-related costs in debt sustainability scenarios. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at -2.1% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 21.6% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 3.1% of GDP improvement in 2027 to stabilize debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 168" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 168">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund was 75 bps at the end of 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 166" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 166">ⓘ</button>
- Under the "Fragmented Action" climate scenario, debt could be around 6 percentage points of GDP higher in 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109">ⓘ</button>
- Economic activity is forecast to grow at 0.8% in 2026 and 1.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 122" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 122">ⓘ</button>
- The general government deficit is forecast to remain at 5.1% in 2026 and rise to 5.7% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 123" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 123">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary deficit before cost of ageing of -3.0% of GDP in 2026, stabilizing at -2.1% from 2027 onwards. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 170" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 170">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator requires a 3.1% of GDP effort to stabilize debt, driven by the initial budgetary position (3.0%) and ageing costs (0.1%). The S1 indicator requires a 3.9% of GDP effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 170" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 170">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are projected at 21.1% of GDP in 2026, rising to 27.8% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 170" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 170">ⓘ</button>

### [Germany](../countries/germany.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) highlights prolonged economic stagnation, with real GDP growth remaining near zero since 2019, and projects modest recovery of 0.6% in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that the general government deficit is projected to rise from 2.7% of GDP in 2025 to 4.1% in 2027, driven by defense spending and infrastructure funds. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission notes that the Council activated the National Escape Clause for Germany to facilitate its transition to higher levels of defense spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 33" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 33">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assesses the implementation of 2025 Country-Specific Recommendations. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 33, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 33, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at -2.1% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 14.3% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assessed the fiscal sustainability condition for activating the NEC. It concluded that sustainability is preserved over the medium term. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 4.1% of GDP improvement in 2027 to stabilize debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 143" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 143">ⓘ</button>
- Under the "Fragmented Action" climate scenario, debt could be around 3 percentage points of GDP higher in 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109">ⓘ</button>
- Real GDP growth is forecast at 0.6% in 2026 and 0.9% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 112" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 112">ⓘ</button>
- The general government deficit is projected to increase to 3.7% of GDP in 2026 and 4.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 113" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 113">ⓘ</button>

### [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) conducted post-programme surveillance missions in March and April 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assesses that [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd) retains the capacity to service its debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assesses Greece’s economy as having grown solidly, with real GDP projected to remain robust at 1.8% in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that Greece recorded a general government budget surplus in 2024 and 2025, projected to narrow to 0.8% in 2026. Public debt is projected to decrease from 146.1% in 2025 to 134.4% by 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 5-6" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 5-6">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission noted that the Council activated the National Escape Clause for Greece to facilitate the transition to higher levels of defense spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 32, p. 36" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 32, p. 36">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission conducted an in-depth review of Greece under the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 32, p. 36" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 32, p. 36">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) cited the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)’s Ageing Report, which projects a decline in ageing-related expenditures in Greece compared to the European average. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) referenced the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)’s Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI), noting Greece’s rapid progress in digitalising public services. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- The outlook remains positive for 2024–2026, supported by rising disbursements from the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)’s Recovery and Resilience Facility (“Greece 2.0”). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at 1.8% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 8.2% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) notes the activation of the national escape clause (NEC) for Greece. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 113">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to low risk, as no improvement relative to the baseline is needed to stabilize debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 158" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 158">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund was 63 bps at the end of 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 157" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 157">ⓘ</button>
- Under the "Fragmented Action" climate scenario, debt could be around 6 percentage points of GDP higher in 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109">ⓘ</button>
- GDP growth is forecast to decelerate to 1.8% in 2026 and 1.6% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 118" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 118">ⓘ</button>
- The general government surplus is set to moderate to 0.8% of GDP in 2026 and 0.6% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 119" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 119">ⓘ</button>

### [Hungary](../countries/hungary.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary deficit of 0.9% of GDP as of 2026. This is low compared with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to increase. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 202" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 202">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to high risk, requiring a 6.7 percentage point improvement. The S1 indicator points to high risk, requiring a 5.3 percentage point effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 203" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 203">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected to increase, reaching around 21% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 202" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 202">ⓘ</button>
- Significant proportion of foreign currency debt exposes the government to exchange rate risk. High exposure of domestic banks to government debt. Sizable amount of redeemable retail government bonds (approx. 20% of central government debt in 2024) poses refinancing risk. High level of contingent liabilities from state guarantees. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 203" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 203">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 408 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 204" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 204">ⓘ</button>

### [Ireland](../countries/ireland.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) conducted post-programme surveillance missions in March and April 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assesses that [Ireland](../countries/ireland.qmd) retains the capacity to service its debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission projects real GDP growth to decline by 1.2% in 2026 due to base effects from the front-loading of pharmaceutical exports in 2025, before stabilizing at 3.4% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission highlights that Ireland’s economy is highly concentrated in multinational corporations, particularly in pharmaceuticals and ICT, creating exposure to firm-specific disruptions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission notes that mainstream political platforms rely heavily on transient corporate tax revenues. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 36" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 36">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assesses that Ireland is compliant with the EU fiscal framework and that the Council endorsed its revised medium-term fiscal-structural plan in March 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 25, p. 31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 25, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that gross government debt decreased to 32.9% of GDP in 2025 and is projected to fall to 31.6% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) references the European Commission’s Ageing Report for economic and budgetary projections for EU Member States from 2022 to 2070. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) cites the European Commission’s assessment of the draft Updated National Energy and Climate Plan of Ireland. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that the European Commission’s debt-sustainability risk classification and compliance record are relevant for backstop eligibility. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that the new EU fiscal rules are not currently a binding constraint for Ireland. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at 1.4% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 2.1% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- Ireland submitted a revised medium-term plan following elections, which was still being assessed at the cut-off date. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 115" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 115">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 3.3% of GDP improvement in 2027 to stabilize debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 153" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 153">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund was 20 bps at the end of 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 152" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 152">ⓘ</button>
- GDP is forecast to decline by 1.2% in 2026 due to base effects from pharmaceutical export frontloading, before growing 3.4% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 116" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 116">ⓘ</button>
- The general government surplus is forecast to decline to 1.4% of GDP in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 117" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 117">ⓘ</button>

### [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) reports that real GDP growth decelerated to 0.5% in 2025 due to geopolitical uncertainty and trade barriers. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission notes that labor productivity stagnation persists, with Italy’s GDP growth lagging behind employment growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that the general government deficit fell to 3.1% of GDP in 2025 but remains above the EU reference value. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 47" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 47">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission projects the debt-to-GDP ratio to rise from 137.1% in 2025 to 139.2% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission undertook an in-depth review of the Italian economy under the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that Italy is subject to an excessive deficit procedure, which is held in abeyance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd)'s Medium-Term Fiscal-Structural Plan aligns with commitments under the revised EU fiscal rules approved by the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at 1.1% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 23.3% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- Real GDP is expected to grow by 0.5% in 2026 and 0.6% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 126" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 126">ⓘ</button>
- The government deficit is projected to fall to 2.9% of GDP in both 2026 and 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 127" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 127">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary surplus of 1.1% of GDP as of 2026. This is broadly in line with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to increase. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 177" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 177">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to low risk, as no improvement is needed to stabilize debt due to projected decreases in ageing costs. The S1 indicator points to low risk, requiring a 1.6% of GDP effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 178" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 178">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected to remain large, reaching around 27% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 177" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 177">ⓘ</button>
- Risk-increasing factors relate to the share of short-term government debt. Risk-mitigating factors include the major share of debt held by domestic lenders and euro denomination. The favourable net international investment position mitigates fiscal risks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 178" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 178">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 74 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 179" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 179">ⓘ</button>

### [Latvia](../countries/latvia.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) reported that Latvia’s economy recovered with real GDP growth of 2.1% in 2025, driven by private consumption and investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission noted that labor productivity reached 62.2% of the EU average in 2025, lagging behind wage growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission projected the general government deficit to widen to 4.3% of GDP in 2027, driven by increased defense spending and labor tax reforms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reported that the Council of the EU activated the national escape clause for Latvia in July 2025 to facilitate the transition to higher levels of defense spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission noted that the general government debt-to-GDP ratio reached 46.9% in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document referenced the European Commission's assessment of Latvia's National Energy and Climate Plan and its data on cohesion policy funding absorption. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 53" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 53">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at -2.1% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 8.7% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- GDP growth is forecast to slow to 1.4% in 2026 and pick up to 1.6% in 2027 due to the Middle East conflict. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 130" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 130">ⓘ</button>
- The general government deficit is forecast to increase to 3.3% of GDP in 2026 and 4.3% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 130" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 130">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary deficit of 2.1% of GDP as of 2026. This is low compared with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to remain stable. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 187" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 187">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 2.2 percentage point improvement. The S1 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 2.4 percentage point effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 188" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 188">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected at around 10% of GDP on average over 2026-2027, rising to around 11% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 187" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 187">ⓘ</button>
- A relatively large share of public debt is held by non-residents. The net international investment position is negative. Risk-mitigating factors include the low share of short-term debt and euro denomination. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 188" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 188">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 85 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 189" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 189">ⓘ</button>

### [Lithuania](../countries/lithuania.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) reports that Lithuania’s real GDP growth reached 2.9% in 2025 and is projected at 3.0% in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission notes that unit labour costs per hour rose sharply in 2022 and 2023, implying risks to cost competitiveness. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 10" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 10">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission projects the general government deficit to rise to 2.7% of GDP in 2027, with public debt increasing to 48.4% of GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that the Council of the EU activated the national escape clause for defense spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission highlights that the 2026 pension reform allowing opt-outs is expected to reduce pension fund assets under management by approximately 41%. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 13, p. 64" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 13, p. 64">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) cites the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s 2024 Ageing Report for projections of ageing-related expenditure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 13" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 13">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at -1.3% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 7.3% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- Real GDP is projected to grow by 3.0% in 2026 and 2.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 132" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 132">ⓘ</button>
- The general government deficit is projected to increase to 2.2% in 2026 and 2.7% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 132" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 132">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary deficit of 1.3% of GDP as of 2026. This is low compared with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to increase. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 192" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 192">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 5.1 percentage point improvement. The S1 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 4.0 percentage point effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 193" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 193">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected to remain low, at around 10% of GDP over 2026-2027, reaching around 11% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 192" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 192">ⓘ</button>
- A relatively large share of public debt is held by non-residents. Risk-mitigating factors include the low share of short-term debt and full euro denomination. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 193" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 193">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 7 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 194" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 194">ⓘ</button>

### [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) reports that real GDP growth slowed to 1.1% in the 2020–2025 period, driven by stagnating labor productivity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission notes that labor productivity decreased by 1.6% per year on average between 2021 and 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that Luxembourg was found not compliant with its medium-term fiscal-structural plan commitments in 2025, with a general government deficit of 2.0% of GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission projects gross general government debt to increase from 26.5% of GDP in 2025 to 30.2% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 37">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission notes that the pension system is projected to start running a deficit as of 2029 due to unfavorable demographic dynamics. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at 1.4% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 3.6% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- Real GDP growth is expected to accelerate to 1.6% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 134" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 134">ⓘ</button>
- The general government balance is forecast to remain in deficit, improving to -1.2% in 2026 and widening slightly to -1.5% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 135" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 135">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary surplus of 1.4% of GDP as of 2026. This is low compared with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to increase. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 197" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 197">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to high risk, requiring a 7.1 percentage point improvement, driven by ageing costs (7.8 pps). The S1 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 2.0 percentage point effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 198" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 198">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected to decrease to around 3% of GDP on average over 2026-2027, reaching around 2% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 197" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 197">ⓘ</button>
- Risk-increasing factors relate to contingent liability risks from the private sector and changes in international financial regulations. Risk-mitigating factors include lengthening debt maturity, stable financing sources, euro denomination, and a positive net international investment position. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 198" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 198">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 29 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 199" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 199">ⓘ</button>

### [Malta](../countries/malta.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assesses [Malta](../countries/malta.qmd)'s economy as robust, driven by strong domestic consumption and tourism, with real gross domestic product (GDP) growth projected at 3.7% for 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that the general government deficit is expected to remain stable at 2.2% of GDP in 2026, supported by a public debt ratio of approximately 46% of GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission highlights key policy challenges including high reliance on foreign labor, persistent skills shortages, and structural issues in the tax system. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4, 10, 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4, 10, 39">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission notes that [Malta](../countries/malta.qmd) has adhered to net expenditure growth rates recommended by the [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd) to address its excessive deficit situation. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 35, 29" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 35, 29">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission has proposed to abrogate the excessive deficit procedure due to compliance with net expenditure growth rates. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at -1.0% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 8.2% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- Real GDP is expected to grow by 3.7% in 2026 and 3.6% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 136" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 136">ⓘ</button>
- The government deficit is forecast to remain stable at 2.2% in 2026 and fall to 2.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 137" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 137">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary deficit of 1% of GDP as of 2026. This is in line with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to decrease slightly over the medium term but increase over the long term. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 207" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 207">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to high risk, requiring an 8.1 percentage point improvement, driven by ageing costs (6.5 pps). The S1 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 3.1 percentage point effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 208" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 208">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected to amount to 7.5% of GDP over 2026-2027, decreasing to 6.5% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 207" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 207">ⓘ</button>
- Risk-mitigating factors include a high share of domestically-held debt and a positive international investment position. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 208" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 208">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 91 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 209" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 209">ⓘ</button>

### [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) reports that the Dutch economy grew by 1.8% in 2025, supported by strong domestic demand. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission projects public finances to remain sound, with the government deficit projected to rise to 2.5% of GDP in 2026 before declining. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission highlights significant challenges in housing supply, labour market segmentation, and the transition to sustainable energy. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 4-6" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 4-6">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission conducted an in-depth review of the Dutch economy under the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3, 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3, 4">ⓘ</button>
- Real gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 2025 was 1.8%. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast projects real GDP to grow by 1.0% in 2026 and 1.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- The [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd) endorsed the national medium-term fiscal-structural plan for the period 2026-2030. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- The fiscal stance was expansionary by 0.8% of GDP in 2025 and is projected to be broadly neutral in 2026 and 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- Net expenditure in the [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd) grew by 7.2% in 2025, above the maximum growth rate recommended by the [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) adopted an opinion on the 2026 draft budgetary plan of the [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 2-3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 2-3">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) published the 2026 country report for the [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd), concluded that the [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd) is no longer experiencing macroeconomic imbalances, and adopted the Spring 2026 Economic Forecast. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 2-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 2-4">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assesses the fiscal stance and net expenditure growth against recommended maximum rates under the EU fiscal framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3-5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3-5">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at -0.6% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 8.9% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- GDP growth is projected to slow to 1.0% in 2026 and 1.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 138" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 138">ⓘ</button>
- The general government deficit is set to increase to 2.5% in 2026 and decrease to 1.9% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 139" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 139">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that the [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd)'s projected path for net primary expenditure growth is higher than the limits assigned by the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd), potentially leading to a "Significant Deviation Procedure" under the EU Stability and Growth Pact. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s debt-sustainability risk classification and fiscal rules are referenced as key constraints on Dutch fiscal policy. [oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 13; <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 3" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 3">ⓘ</button>8]
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary deficit of 0.6% of GDP as of 2026. This is low compared with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to increase. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 212" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 212">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 3.9 percentage point improvement. The S1 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 2.5 percentage point effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 213" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 213">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs are expected to remain moderate, at around 10% of GDP over 2026-2027, reaching 13% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 212" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 212">ⓘ</button>
- Risk-increasing factors relate to relatively large contingent liabilities. Risk-mitigating factors include lengthening debt maturity, stable financing sources, and a very large share of debt denominated in euro. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 213" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 213">ⓘ</button>
- The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 16 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 214" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 214">ⓘ</button>

### [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) conducted post-programme surveillance missions in March and April 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission assesses that [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd) retains the capacity to service its debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission highlights solid economic growth outpacing the euro-area average, driven by domestic consumption and investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3-4, p. 50, p. 56" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3-4, p. 50, p. 56">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that public debt declined to 89.7% of GDP in 2025, with a general government surplus of 0.7% of GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission projects a shift to a small deficit in 2026–2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission emphasizes key fiscal challenges including rising pension costs due to an aging population. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5-6, p. 41-42, p. 45-48" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5-6, p. 41-42, p. 45-48">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission notes that the [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd) activated the "national escape clause" for [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd) in July 2025 to facilitate higher defense spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 34" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast projects real GDP growth of 1.7% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd) recorded a general government surplus of 0.7% of GDP in 2025. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a deficit of 0.1% of GDP in 2026 and 0.4% of GDP in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- Net expenditure grew by 5.5% in 2025 and is projected to grow by 5.6% in 2026. Both figures exceed the recommended maximum growth rates. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 4-5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 4-5">ⓘ</button>
- The fiscal stance was broadly neutral in 2025, projected to be expansionary by 1.6% of GDP in 2026, and contractionary by 1.3% of GDP in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) highlights sustainability pressures on the pay-as-you-go pension system due to population ageing. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- General government debt decreased from 93.5% of GDP in 2024 to 89.7% of GDP in 2025. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a further decrease to 87.6% in 2026 and 86.0% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd) endorsed [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd)'s national medium-term fiscal-structural plan on 21 January 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at 1.8% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 9.7% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- The S2 debt-stabilisation indicator points to low risk. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 228" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 228">ⓘ</button>
- The S1 debt-reduction indicator points to low risk. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 228" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 228">ⓘ</button>
- Financial markets’ perceptions of sovereign risk are investment grade, with a 10-year sovereign yield spread of 33 basis points versus the German Bund as of December 31, 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 227, 229" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 227, 229">ⓘ</button>
- GDP growth is forecast to drop marginally to 1.7% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 142" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 142">ⓘ</button>
- The general government surplus is forecast to turn into a small deficit of 0.1% in 2026 and 0.4% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 143" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 143">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assessed Portugal’s draft updated National Energy and Climate Plan. It also urges [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd) to fully transpose EU rules accelerating permitting procedures for renewable energy projects. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 92" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 92">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) reported implementation delays in public transport projects funded by the Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 95" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 95">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) estimated investment needs to fully transform [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd)’s building stock at EUR 4.95 billion per year. Current funding, including EUR 300 million from the Recovery and Resilience Plan, falls short of these needs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 137" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 137">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s 2024 Ageing Report provides projections for ageing-related costs, which the OECD uses to illustrate long-term fiscal pressures. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) also oversees the implementation of the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34">ⓘ</button>

### [Slovakia](../countries/slovakia.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) highlights weak economic growth, driven by fiscal consolidation and an unfavorable external environment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission reports that the general government deficit reached 4.5% of GDP in 2025 and is projected to rise to 5.4% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission notes that Slovakia’s fiscal strategy relies heavily on tax increases, which burden competitiveness. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission underscores the need for a comprehensive fiscal strategy, improvements in the business environment, and accelerated progress in the green and digital transitions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission issued Country-Specific Recommendations (CSRs) and monitored the implementation of the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 1, 3, 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 1, 3, 5">ⓘ</button>
- The [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd) endorsed [Slovakia](../countries/slovakia.qmd)'s national medium-term fiscal-structural plan in January 2025. - Net expenditure grew by 1.7% in 2025, below the recommended maximum. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- The excessive deficit procedure for [Slovakia](../countries/slovakia.qmd) is held in abeyance following the endorsement of its fiscal-structural plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The structural primary balance is projected at -2.6% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Gross financing needs were 10.1% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- Long-term fiscal sustainability risks are high. - Financial markets’ perceptions of sovereign risk are investment grade, but a recent downgrade reflects broad institutional challenges and political tensions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 242" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 242">ⓘ</button>
- Real GDP growth is expected to remain modest at 0.8% in 2026, picking up to 1.5% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 146" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 146">ⓘ</button>
- The public deficit is projected to rise to 4.6% in 2026 and 5.4% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 146" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 146">ⓘ</button>
- The European Commission notified a reversal of a milestone in April 2024 regarding the approval of national expenditure ceilings under the EU Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48, 88" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48, 88">ⓘ</button>

- The Commission reports that the Council of the European Union activated the 'national escape clause' for Slovenia to facilitate higher defense spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 39">ⓘ</button>

- The general government deficit increased from 0.9% of GDP in 2024 to 2.5% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The fiscal stance was expansionary by 1.6% of GDP in 2025, projected to be expansionary by 1.3% in 2026, and contractionary by 0.7% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- Net expenditure grew by 8.8% in 2025 and is projected to grow by 7.2% in 2026, both above the recommended maximum growth rates. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Council activated the national escape clause for [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd) for the period 2025-2028. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>

- The structural primary balance is projected at -1.3% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41">ⓘ</button>

- The government deficit is projected to widen to 3.3% of GDP in 2026 and 3.5% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 144" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 144">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assessed the 2026 Draft Budgetary Plan of [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd) as at risk of non-compliance with the maximum growth of net expenditure allowed by the fiscal plan, though within the control account threshold after using flexibility from the national escape clause. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30">ⓘ</button>

- Following the outbreak of war in the Middle East in February 2026, Spain adopted fiscal policy measures to mitigate high energy prices. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- Net expenditure grew by 4.8% in 2025, exceeding the recommended maximum growth rate. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Council endorsed Spain’s national medium-term fiscal-structural plan covering 2025–2028. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- Spain activated the national escape clause of the Stability and Growth Pact for the period 2025–2028. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>

- Spain is subject to the preventive arm of the Stability and Growth Pact under Regulation (EU) 2024/1263. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1-2" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1-2">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) adopted the recommendation for the Council Recommendation. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1-3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1-3">ⓘ</button>
